title: A Song of Types and Agents - Roberto Stagi, Ratel
talk_summary: A conference talk arguing that TypeScript, not Python, is becoming the default language for building AI agents at the application layer, because coding agents are trained on it, NPM is rich, and one language/schema (Zod) can span agent loop, backend, and UI. It is a language-ecosystem opinion piece with no agent-orchestration, cost, review, or reliability techniques.

takeaways.technique: Single-language, single-schema stack for agent + backend + UI
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues for keeping the agent loop, tools, backend, and UI in one TypeScript codebase with one Zod schema shared end-to-end, avoiding a Python/React split and a hand-maintained contract between services.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You can define a type once. You can use this type in the back end and uh in the model, and you can use the same type in your UI.
